While I was trying to sleep, she kept texting me with things I needed to do. I tried to ignore it and turned off my phone's notifications so I could get some sleep. Around an hour later, she called me and told me I had to send her a file (regarding clients' data which she doesn't have on her laptop) immediately as it was an urgent matter. I sent her the files she wanted and asked her if she'd need anything else as I was going to the doctor and wouldn't be bringing my laptop with me. She said that was all for now. I went to the doctor, and the doctor said I was overworked (I've been working overtime till 2-3 AM for the past two months) and needed some rest. On my way home, my senior associate again texted me and told me to get our clients' billing information (something she could do herself as she also has their contacts). I did as I was told and forwarded her with the information. I got home, took the prescribed medicine, and fell asleep. I was shocked when I woke up to find my phone with two missed calls and 30 new messages from her giving me work to do from home. I felt it was a little bit unfair of her to give me work while I was on sick leave and so I ignored the message and didn't reply her. Now, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to ignore her texts? And why? First, I need to consider the context. I was sick, overworked, and the doctor advised me to rest. Ignoring her texts allowed me to get the rest I needed. On the other hand, she might have felt that the work was urgent and needed my attention. I also need to think about the power dynamics between a first-year associate and a senior associate. She has been with the firm longer and might feel responsible for ensuring tasks are completed, even if it means contacting me while I'm on sick leave. Additionally, I should consider the company's policies regarding sick leave and communication during such periods. If there's a clear policy, that could guide whether ignoring her texts was appropriate. Another aspect is the impact on my health. By ignoring her texts, I prioritized my well-being, which is important, especially since I was overworked. However, ignoring her texts might have led to delays in completing tasks or could have strained our working relationship. It's also possible that she felt the need to contact me because she didn't have the necessary information herself, which might indicate a lack of preparedness on her part. I also need to think about how I would feel if the roles were reversed. If I were the senior associate, would I expect my junior associate to respond to texts while on sick leave? Probably not, as rest is crucial for recovery. Moreover, communication is key in such situations. If I had responded to her texts to explain that I was unwell and would be unable to work, it might have prevented misunderstandings. In summary, while ignoring her texts allowed me to rest and recover, it might have had negative consequences in terms of work completion and team dynamics. It's a balance between self-care and fulfilling professional responsibilities. I also need to consider cultural and organizational norms. In some cultures, work-life balance is highly valued, and taking sick leave is respected. In others, there might be an expectation to be available even when unwell. Additionally, I should reflect on whether there were alternative ways to handle the situation. For example, could I have set up an auto-reply or informed her in advance that I wouldn't be available to respond to texts while I was resting? Lastly, it's important to think about how to prevent such situations in the future. Managing workload, setting boundaries, and communicating clearly with colleagues can help avoid similar conflicts. Overall, while ignoring her texts was a way to prioritize my health, it's essential to find a balance that respects both personal well-being and professional responsibilities.
